title: Add sandboxed extension system with permission-based security
summary: Settings › Extensions is redesigned: extensions are listed under **Installed** and **Available** with a search box, each one opens its own page (About, plus Permissions and Settings tabs once installed), and a new **Add extensions from a link** button adds outside extensions. Extensions added from a link now run walled off from the rest of the app and only get the permissions you approve in a new consent dialog. The old Download/Upload Extensions buttons are gone.

links.label: How extension security works (docs in this PR)

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email address (you'll be sent a code, so use an inbox you can check). Extension settings are saved to your account, so several tests need you signed in.

setup.title: Find Settings › Extensions
setup.body: Open **Settings**, then **Extensions**. This is the screen most tests start from.

tests.title: Extensions are split into Installed and Available
steps: Open **Settings** › **Extensions**.
Look at the list.
expected: There's a **Search extensions** box at the top, then an **Installed** heading and an **Available** heading, each with its own list.
Each row shows the extension's icon, name and a short description, with an arrow on the right. Extensions that come with Seed Bible show a **Built in** tag.
There are no **Download Extensions** or **Upload Extensions** buttons any more. An **Add extensions from a link** button sits below the list.

tests.title: Searching narrows the list
steps: Type `apol` in **Search extensions**.
Clear the box, then type `zzzz`.
expected: With `apol`, only **Apologist** is listed (a section with no matches is left out).
With `zzzz`, the list is replaced by **No extensions match “zzzz”.**
Clearing the box brings the full list back.

tests.title: Each extension opens its own page
steps: Click any built-in extension under **Available**.
Look at the page, then use the back arrow at the top.
expected: A page for that extension opens with its icon and name, **Built into Seed Bible** under the name, its description, an **Install** button and a **Details** section (with **ID**, and **Version** if it has one).
The breadcrumb at the top reads **Page settings › Extensions › <extension name>**.
Back returns you to the Extensions list.

sections.title: Installing, configuring and removing a built-in extension

tests.title: Installing a built-in extension moves it to Installed
steps: Under **Available**, open **Apologist** (or another built-in extension if it isn't listed).
Click **Install**.
expected: The button briefly shows **Installing…**, then the page shows an **Installed** label with a check mark next to the name.
Tabs appear: **About** and **Settings**. The **Install** button is replaced by **Uninstall Apologist** at the bottom of About.
Going back to the list, Apologist is now under **Installed**. No consent dialog appears for a built-in extension.

tests.title: An extension's settings are on its Settings tab
tests.why: The old **Configure** button on each row was replaced by this tab.
tests.before: Apologist is installed from the previous test.
steps: Open **Apologist** from **Installed** and choose the **Settings** tab.
Change one of its text settings, go back to the list, then open Apologist's **Settings** tab again.
expected: The Settings tab shows Apologist's settings form.
Your change is still there when you come back. No **Couldn't save your settings.** message appears.

tests.title: Signed out, the Settings tab asks you to log in
steps: Sign out, then open **Settings** › **Extensions** › **Apologist** › **Settings**.
expected: The tab shows **Please log in to configure this extension.** and a **Log in** button instead of the form.
Signing in from there swaps the message for the form.

tests.title: Uninstalling moves the extension back to Available
steps: Open **Apologist** from **Installed** and click **Uninstall Apologist** on the About tab.
Reload the page and check Settings › Extensions again.
expected: The page goes back to showing **Install**, with no Installed label and no tabs.
In the list, and after reloading, Apologist is under **Available**.

tests.title: The link dialog explains itself and starts focused
steps: In **Settings** › **Extensions**, click **Add extensions from a link** below the list.
expected: A dialog titled **Add extensions from a link** opens with a **Link** box (showing `https://` as a placeholder), a greyed-out **Add** button, and the hint **Paste the link an extension's developer gave you. Nothing is installed until you choose to.**
The cursor is already in the Link box, so you can type straight away. **Add** becomes clickable once you've typed something.

tests.title: A link with no extensions shows a clear error
steps: In the dialog, type `https://example.com` and click **Add**.
Then try `http://example.com` (without the s).
expected: Both times the hint is replaced by **Couldn't find any extensions at that link. Check that it's the full https:// link.**
Nothing is added to the Extensions list, and the app doesn't freeze or show a blank screen.

sections.title: Installing an outside (sandboxed) extension
sections.intro: These need a link to a published extension, because nothing in the app ships one.

setup.title: Get an extension link
setup.body: Ask the PR author (or check the PR comments) for the link to the published **Sandboxed Example Extension**. If nobody can give you one, mark every test in this section **Blocked** and say so in the note.

tests.title: Adding a one-extension link opens that extension's page
steps: Open **Add extensions from a link**, paste the link you were given and click **Add**.
expected: The dialog closes and the **Sandboxed Example Extension** page opens.
Under the name it says **Version 1.0.0 · from <the link's website>** (and who uploaded it, if it was uploaded to Seed Bible's storage) instead of **Built into Seed Bible**.
A notice says **Seed Bible hasn't reviewed this extension. It runs separately and only gets what's listed here.**
**What it can do** lists **See which passage you're reading** under **Right away**, and **Show CasualOS maps and grids** under **Only if you agree later**.

tests.title: Cancelling the consent dialog doesn't install anything
steps: On the Sandboxed Example Extension page, click **Install**.
Read the dialog, then click **Cancel**.
expected: A dialog titled **Install Sandboxed Example Extension?** lists what it'll get right away and what it may ask for later, with **Install** and **Cancel** buttons.
After **Cancel**, the extension is still not installed: the page still shows **Install** and it's listed under **Available**.

tests.title: Approving installs it and its tools appear
steps: Click **Install** again and choose **Install** in the dialog.
Close Settings and look at the reader's tool buttons.
expected: The page shows **Installed**, with **About**, **Permissions** and **Settings** tabs.
New tools appear in the reader, such as **My Example Tool**, and clicking it opens the extension's panel without errors.

tests.title: Asking for a permission later shows a request dialog
steps: Click the **Open grid portal** tool.
In the dialog that appears, click **Not now**.
Click **Open grid portal** again and this time click **Allow**.
expected: A dialog asks **Sandboxed Example Extension wants access to maps and 3D experiences**, saying it won't remove the extension if you say no.
After **Not now**, a short message says **Showing a CasualOS portal needs your permission.** and no portal opens.
After **Allow**, a grid portal opens in a panel.

tests.title: The Permissions tab shows and changes what it's allowed
steps: Open **Settings** › **Extensions** › **Sandboxed Example Extension** › **Permissions**.
Turn off the maps permission you allowed in the previous test.
expected: **See which passage you're reading** is marked **Needed** and can't be turned off; a note says to uninstall to remove it.
Turning off the maps permission shows **Saved. Sandboxed Example Extension restarted with the new permissions.** Clicking **Open grid portal** asks again.

tests.title: The extension is still installed after a reload
steps: Reload the page and look for **My Example Tool** in the reader.
Open **Settings** › **Extensions**.
expected: The tool is still there, and the extension is still under **Installed** with no consent dialog shown again.

tests.title: Uninstalling removes it and its tools
steps: Open the extension's page and click **Uninstall Sandboxed Example Extension**.
Close Settings and reload.
expected: Its tools disappear from the reader, and after reloading they don't come back.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Extensions you already had still load and work
steps: Use an extension you had installed before this PR (for example **Compare** or **References**) as you normally would.
expected: It's listed under **Installed** and works as before.

tests.title: The Extensions screen fits a phone-width window
steps: Make the browser window as narrow as a phone (or open the preview on a phone).
Open **Settings** › **Extensions**, then one extension's page and its tabs.
expected: Nothing is cut off or needs scrolling sideways; the tabs and buttons fit on screen.

tests.title: The Extensions screen reads well in dark mode
steps: Switch Seed Bible to dark mode and open **Settings** › **Extensions** and an extension's page.
expected: All text, tags, tabs and the link button are readable against the dark background.

notCovered: The developer tools added for extension authors (create-seed-bible-extension and seed-bible-extension-scripts: check, build, dev, test, publish).

Most individual sandbox permissions (highlights, notes, chat, friends, clipboard, microphone, camera, audio), which only an extension that asks for them can show; these are covered by automated tests.
Opening an install link of the form ?extensionSet=… directly, which needs a published extension link too.
Extension storage syncing between devices, and the developer documentation.
